The clinical picture of painless jaundice, significant weight loss, and pale stools, combined with a soft, cystic mass in the right upper quadrant and markedly elevated direct bilirubin with high alkaline phosphatase, is diagnostic for a malignant obstruction of the biliary tree. The normal liver enzymes (AST/ALT) rule out primary hepatitis or acute cholecystitis, and the lack of fever makes acute cholangitis unlikely.
